title: Add mutation_log table for critical-table writes (data-loss step 3)
description:
Defends against the dominant threat in this codebase: our own code corrupting our own data via buggy mutations (centroid bug, Company Enrich silent failure, phone column inversion all had this shape). Backups don't help here because we back up the bad data right after writing it.

What to do:
- New mutation_log table: id, ts, actor (user/script), table_name, row_id, op (insert/update/delete), before_json, after_json
- Add a tiny LogMutationMixin in db/_mutation_log.py with log_mutation() helper
- Instrument the high-value mutation sites: operators (create/update/delete), staged_exports (insert/mark_exported/mark_pushed), lead_outcomes (update). NOT every table — just the ones where surprise mutations cause operator pain.
- Index on (table_name, ts) for cheap recent-history queries
- A retention policy: keep 90 days, purged by the same weekly sweeper from step 2
- Add a Pipeline Health panel showing last 20 mutations + a 'undo' button surface for a future bead

Why: the actual undo button against our own bad writes. Append-only, cheap at our scale (~hundreds of writes/day across 5 operators), genuinely diagnostic when something goes wrong ("what changed on operators table this morning?"). Effort ~4h.

title: Architect data-loss defenses (threat-model driven)
description:
Parent epic for data-loss defenses, scoped from the systems-architect analysis on 2026-05-19 (see CODE_REVIEW_2026-05-18.md follow-up discussion).

Reframing: the dominant data-loss threat in this codebase is NOT cloud-provider failure — it is OUR OWN CODE corrupting OUR OWN DATA via migration bugs, silent-failure writes, accidental deletes. A traditional backup script protects against the rarest threats (account loss, engine crash) and not the common ones (we happily back up the bad data we just wrote).

This epic ships four small, independent defenses that target the actual threat model. Closure: when all 4 children close.

title: No phone↔company integrity check; entity-swapped records pass through silently
